name: Protected-Certificate Depth
definition: For a nonpeelable ample family $L$, a protected set is a subset $S$ with at least two vertices such that every $x\in S$ has a coordinate set $J_x$ whose single-coordinate neighbours $x^{\{e\}}$, $e\in J_x$, all lie in $S$, while $x^{J_x}\notin L$. A corner-choice proof tree branches over every currently available corner deletion and may stop only when the remaining family contains a protected set. The protected-certificate depth $d_{\mathrm{prot}}(L)$ is the minimum, over all such proof trees, of the maximum number of deletions on a branch.
normalization: The root counts zero deletions. The protected set may depend on the leaf. For a finite nonpeelable ample family the value is finite, because a maximal corner-deletion sequence ends at a nonempty cornerless family, which is protected.
comments: This measures a specific branching certificate based on protected missing cubes. It is not the minimum length of an arbitrary proof of nonpeelability.
